claims.wikipedia_text_verbatim: The Indus Valley Civilisation (IVC), also known as the Indus Civilisation, was a Bronze Age civilisation in the northwestern regions of South Asia, lasting from 3300 BCE to 1300 BCE, and in its mature form from 2600 BCE to 1900 BCE.

citation_footnotes_verbatim.a: Wright: 'Mesopotamia and Egypt ... co-existed with the Indus civilization during its florescence between 2600 and 1900 BC.'

source.author: Rita P. Wright
source.title: The Ancient Indus: Urbanism, Economy, and Society

verbatim_quotes: Mesopotamia and Egypt ... co-existed with the Indus civilization during its florescence between 2600 and 1900 BC.

citation_chain.cited_by: Kenoyer (1991) identified independently as the source of the HARP radiocarbon chronology underlying Wright (2009)

source.author: Jonathan Mark Kenoyer
source.title: Urban Process in the Indus Tradition: A Preliminary Model from Harappa
source.container_work: Harappa Excavations 1986-1990: A Multidisciplinary Approach to Third Millennium Urbanism, ed. Richard H. Meadow

verbatim_quotes: At the present time, a total of 33 carbon samples from the recent excavations at Harappa have been dated ... This sample date is calibrated to 3338, 3213, or 3203 BC (CALIB program, Stuiver and Reimer 1986; Possehl 1990b).
The date 2600 BC is now considered to mark the approximate beginning of the major integration of urban polities, the use of writing, weights, Harappan type ceramic designs, etc.
However, at Harappa there are between one and two meters of Period 3 occupation levels above the uppermost dated levels, which would suggest that Period 3 continues to 1900 BC, if not later.

claims.wikipedia_text_verbatim: In 2019, a study was published by Shinde et al. on a reconstructed genome obtained from a female skeleton found in an IVC-related cemetery in Rakhigarhi, Haryana, India, dating to around 2,800-2,300 BCE.

author: Vasant Shinde
Vagheesh M. Narasimhan
et al.
source.title: An Ancient Harappan Genome Lacks Ancestry from Steppe Pastoralists or Iranian Farmers

verbatim_quotes: The collagen preservation for the human bones at Rakhigarhi cemetery is so poor that Accelerator Mass Spectrometry radiocarbon dating on skeletal remains is very difficult.
Seven dates from charcoal at depths of 9-23 m have point estimates of 2800-2300 BCE, which largely fall within the mature phase of the IVC (Shinde et al., 2018; Vahia et al., 2016).
